title: Checking Your Own Credit Score Does Not Lower It

beats.say: Checking your own credit score never lowers it. Here is what actually damages your score.
beats.visual: a closed metal mailbox covered in dust on a quiet street, wide shot, no people

beats.say: The difference is one word: soft versus hard.
beats.visual: an old brass magnifying glass resting on a closed ledger, soft window light

beats.say: Here is the difference. A soft inquiry is a look. A hard inquiry is a lender's decision check.
beats.visual: two doors in a dim corridor, one slightly open with warm light, no people

beats.say: When you check your own score, or a company checks it for pre approval, that is a soft look.
beats.visual: a quiet window at night with a single lit lamp inside, no people

beats.say: A soft look does not lower your score.
beats.visual: a feather resting on the surface of a perfectly still dark lake, close-up

beats.say: A hard inquiry happens when you apply for new credit, like a card or a loan.
beats.visual: a heavy rubber stamp resting on a stack of papers, dramatic side light

beats.say: That can lower your score by a small amount, often under five points, for a while.
beats.visual: a thin crack in a small clay pot, extreme close-up, warm light

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. Not looking does not protect your score. It only hides mistakes.
beats.visual: a dusty mirror covered by a heavy cloth in a dark attic, no people

beats.say: Errors on a report can cost you real money, and you will never know unless you look.
beats.visual: a single wrong page torn from a ledger lying on a wooden floor, no text

beats.say: You can get your reports for free every week at the official site, annual credit report dot com.
beats.visual: a quiet desk with a laptop open in morning light, no people

beats.say: The honest catch: applying for many cards at once adds several hard inquiries, and that adds up.
beats.visual: a stack of identical empty cardboard boxes in a dim warehouse, no people

beats.say: So look as often as you like. Apply only when you mean to.
beats.visual: a calm hand opening a window to morning light, close-up, no face

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot

caption: Checking your own credit score is a soft inquiry and does not lower it. Applying for new credit is a hard inquiry. The myth, the rule and the catch. Educational content, not financial advice.
description: Many people avoid looking at their own credit score because they think it lowers it. Checking your own score is a soft inquiry and does not hurt it. The myth, the rule and the honest catch.
first_comment: Did you believe this one? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: Checking your own credit score or report is a soft inquiry and does not affect your score
facts.basis: myFICO; CFPB 'Will checking my credit score hurt it?'

facts.claim: A hard inquiry from a lender can lower scores by a small amount (often under 5 points for FICO) for a time
Rate-shopping for a mortgage/auto loan within a short window counts as one inquiry
You can get free weekly credit reports at AnnualCreditReport.com
